events: Marvel identifies Komodo as Hardball's true love; she discovers he has secretly served HYDRA.
Taskmaster assembles a team including Komodo to retake Negative Zone prison 42; she questions whether the operation is suicidal.
Marvel explicitly describes War Machine and Gauntlet jointly leading recruits against HYDRA forces.
War Machine and his assault team pursue the unregistered Spider-Man.
During a training mishap, MVP pushes Cloud 9 out of the path of Armory's blast and is killed.
Armory accidentally shoots and kills the original MVP during a training exercise.
Trauma assumes a frightening form, triggering Armory's panic and uncontrolled discharge.
Gyrich supervises the response to MVP's death; Armory is expelled and deprived of her alien weapon.
Avengers: The Initiative (2007) #1; Secret Invasion (2008) revelation
The administrator and the person presenting as Yellowjacket participate in concealing MVP's death; Marvel later identifies the Yellowjacket serving in the Initiative as Skrull Criti Noll.
Marvel says the Skrull Pym impersonator weaponizes Janet Van Dyne as a biological threat during the invasion.
Marvel says Criti Noll nearly kills Reed Richards while posing as Hank Pym.
Marvel says Beast recruits a former mutant to train Trauma; independent character histories identify the instructor as Dani Moonstar.
Avengers: The Initiative Special (2008) #1; Avengers: The Initiative (2007) #30
The special promises a revelation about Trauma's ancestry; a detailed recap of #30 identifies Nightmare as his biological father and describes possession of Trauma.
Trauma counsels Penance (Robert Baldwin) and tries to help him confront his suppressed memories of Stamford.
After the Nightmare confrontation, Justice offers Penance and Trauma an opportunity to join the Avengers Resistance; they decline.
A detailed issue review describes Hardball amputating Komodo's poisoned legs to prevent toxin spread during KIA's attack.
claims: Marvel calls Komodo Hardball's true love.
Historical relationship; does not establish continued partnership after his HYDRA exposure.
Komodo discovers Hardball has concealed his HYDRA affiliation.
Breach of trust inferred from the revelation; her precise feelings require panels.
An independent issue review reports Hardball amputating poisoned tissue to save Komodo.
A drastic rescue in one incident; not a standing power over her body.
Taskmaster assigns Komodo to his prison-recovery squad.
Operational command for a specific mission; not personal loyalty.
War Machine co-leads a HYDRA engagement with Gauntlet.
Joint field leadership; no inferred personal friendship.
Gauntlet co-leads the recruits with War Machine.
Same event supports reverse participation, not equal rank.
War Machine pursues the unregistered Spider-Man.
Government mission; no permanent personal hatred implied.
MVP moves Cloud 9 out of danger during a training accident.
One fatal protective act, not a sustained guardianship.
Armory accidentally kills MVP with the Tactigon.
Non-volitional fatal consequence; must NOT be coded as deliberate conflict or betrayal.
Trauma's frightening transformation precipitates Armory's panic.
Accidental causal influence, not intentional intimidation.
Armory is expelled after the death under Gyrich's administration.
Exact individual decision and weapon-removal authority need panels.
Gyrich and the person then presenting as Yellowjacket participate in the MVP-death cover-up.
The true Pym must not inherit the impersonator's actions; collaboration is reconstructed across sources.
Criti Noll turns Janet into a biological weapon during Secret Invasion.
Weaponization is directly documented by Marvel; not a consensual alliance.
Marvel says Criti Noll nearly kills Reed Richards.
Specific attack, not a permanent emotional state.
Dani Moonstar is identified in independent character histories as Trauma's trainer.
Marvel issue synopsis confirms an unnamed former-mutant trainer, not the name; identity requires panel check.
Issue recaps identify Nightmare as Trauma's biological father.
Biological relation is secondary-sourced; does not imply care or affection.
Nightmare possesses Trauma to act in the physical world.
Bodily control, not voluntary allegiance; source is an issue recap.
Trauma provides Penance with counseling about his suppressed past.
Therapeutic professional guidance; not proof treatment succeeded.
Justice invites Penance to join the Avengers Resistance.
Invitation declined; do not record membership or reciprocal loyalty.
identity_warnings: Criti Noll is the Skrull impersonating Hank Pym/Yellowjacket during the Initiative; do not attribute 2007 Initiative actions to the real Hank Pym without chronology-specific proof.
MVP Michael Van Patrick is the original recruit killed in #1, not his clones (including KIA or the Scarlet Spiders).
Robert Baldwin is Speedball and Penance, not two separate people.
The original #1 death and cover-up details come from independent issue summaries, not Marvel synopsis or original panels.
Trauma is Terrance Ward, not the similarly named Hulk antagonist.
Marvel #3 calls Trauma's instructor an unnamed former mutant; Dani Moonstar identification is secondary-sourced.
A training accident does not establish intentional hostility; an invitation does not establish acceptance.
Prior uncommitted batch deduplication is not exhaustive; proposed IDs are canonical-absent only.
